extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH grant applications (PHS398) involving vertebrate animals, select agents, and subcontracts (e.g., R21/R33 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Completing the PHS398 Vertebrate Animals and related sections of an NIH grant application: specify animal species/strains, ages, sex, numbers, justification, veterinary care, pain/minimization procedures, euthanasia methods, and any select-agent or consortium compliance. Includes supporting letters and subcontract descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of animal use and group sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide species/strain, ages, sex, and numbers of animals to be used in the proposed work (e.g., 'Vaginal irritation analysis — Rabbits (NZW) — 10-20 wk — F — 27 total (Yr 5 only)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear breakdown by experimental group (control and each dose level), N per group, and total animals/year. Show how groups map to planned outcomes (e.g., n=6 per group except N9 group n=3). If reporting multi-year usage, provide year-by-year counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for animal use, species choice, and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS398: Justify the use of animals, the choice of species, and the numbers to be used. If animals are in short supply, costly, or to be used in large numbers, provide an additional rationale for their selection and numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scientific/regulatory rationale for the chosen model (example: FDA guidance requires testing topical microbicides in the rabbit vaginal irritation (RVI) assay; RVI is considered the 'gold standard'). Explain why in vitro alternatives are inadequate (complex tissue/immune/flora interplay). State basis for group size (e.g., 'small group size (n=6) that is standard in RVI studies' with citations). If preliminary data are limited, explain that initial experiments will inform sample-size re-evaluation and commit to consulting a biostatistician to adjust sample sizes if high variance is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care and institutional assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS398: Provide information on the veterinary care of the animals involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional accreditation and oversight (e.g., AAALAC accreditation), availability of certified veterinarians, Animal Welfare Assurance number with OLAW/PHS, USDA registration number, AAALAC file number, and descriptions/quotations of how animals are cared for and handled. State compliance with the Animal Welfare Act and PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and describe the facility's experience (e.g., GLP capabilities, infectious disease research support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing pain, distress, and use of analgesia/anesthesia
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS398: Describe the procedures for ensuring that discomfort, distress, pain, and injury will be limited to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research. Describe the use of analgesic, anesthetic, and tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices, where appropriate, to minimize discomfort, distress, pain, and injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific procedural details (e.g., sedation before vaginal administration to prevent dislodgement and permit supine positioning). List drugs, routes, and dosages planned (example options given: droperidol/fentanyl IM at 0.125–0.3 ml/kg with solution concentrations noted, or acepromazine 0.25–0.75 mg/kg IM). Describe restraint methods, dosing schedule, monitoring, delivery technique (e.g., 1 ml intravaginally via sterilized needle to 6–8 cm depth for 14 consecutive days), and endpoints for humane intervention. Include how discomfort will be assessed and mitigated during the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia methods and AVMA consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS398: Describe any method of euthanasia to be used and the reasons for its selection. State whether this method is consistent with the recommendations of the Panel on Euthanasia of the American Veterinary Medical Association. If not, present a justification for not following the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the routine euthanasia method (example: intravenous sodium pentobarbital overdose followed by auscultation of the heart) and cite compliance with AVMA reports/guidelines (e.g., 2000 Report and 2007 AVMA guidelines). Describe the circumstances under which euthanasia will be performed (study-design time point, meeting study end-point criteria per ACUP, or unexpected complications determined by veterinarian/study director). If treatment would compromise study integrity and cannot be provided, describe decision process for euthanasia in consultation with veterinarian and project manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent program registration, approvals, and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Select Agent Program: Institutional registration and compliance with CDC Select Agent Program requirements, including IBC approval for non-toxin select agents and annual declarations of select agent toxin possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document current institutional registration status with the CDC Select Agent Program. Describe required approvals (IBC), and administrative processes (annual toxin declarations). Describe facility-level containment (e.g., BSL-3 containment laboratory with keycard-only and alarmed access), compliance with CDC/NIH 'Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories' (BMBL) and select agent requirements, physical security measures for storage, inventory control and reconciliation procedures, periodic review by Select Agent Responsible Official/Biosafety Officer, maintenance of training records and select agent use approvals. State that all personnel working with select agents must be registered with the IBC and federal authorities and that trainees receive hands-on and record-keeping training prior to initiating experiments. If no select agents are used, state that explicitly and commit to providing information if that changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/subcontract agreements and NIH policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe consortia/contractual arrangements (e.g., subcontracts with other universities) and confirm awareness and readiness to establish inter-organizational agreements consistent with NIH consortium agreement policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details for each subcontract including scope (which phases/years supported), responsibilities of subcontract PI(s), detailed budget, percent effort, and deliverables. State that programmatic and administrative personnel at all organizations are aware of NIH consortium policy and prepared to establish necessary inter-organizational agreements. Identify key personnel at subcontract sites, their qualifications, and specific tasks (e.g., synthesis and in vitro evaluation, in vivo testing, specific assays to be supervised).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support documenting consultants' expertise and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters of support from consultants/collaborators that document their willingness to participate, specific roles, expertise, and commitments (e.g., review annual progress reports, participate in data evaluations, provide technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should state the consultant's qualifications, specific technical contributions (e.g., perform cervical explant toxicity assays, supervise rabbit vaginal irritation model), time/effort commitment (percent effort or duration), resources to be provided, and agreement to participate in annual evaluations and progress reporting. Use letters to demonstrate access to specialized assays/models and to confirm collaborators' readiness to support the project milestones.
